language.title: Language
language.help: The language used for the app UI and for the characters. Text the AI newly writes — character lines, diaries, award speeches — follows this too (already-written text stays as it is).

general.summarizerHelp: Summarizes the task label above each head with the chosen summarizer. Uses that account's quota (or API credits).
general.diaryHelp: Each character writes a work log / diary in their own voice at the end of every session (the manual ‘Write diary’ button still works). It calls the same CLI as the summarizer above, so it uses account quota. Read it from the tab's right-click menu.
general.observerHelp: Alerts and timing for Claude, Codex and Pi apply to terminals created from now on. When off, the exclamation alert and session timing do not work.
general.openrouterNote: OpenRouter summaries use an API key (or the OPENROUTER_API_KEY variable). Without a key the summary fails and the raw text is shown.
general.opencodeNote: opencode summaries call the installed opencode CLI. Model ids use provider/model form (see opencode models), and the default assumes opencode's own plan (opencode-go).
general.commandHelp: Command to run for summaries. Leave empty to run {{command}}. You can point this at a wrapper script for a separate account, or at an absolute path — one program only, no arguments.
general.lightModelHelp: Model used for task labels and character diaries. Leave empty for the default ({{model}}).
general.heavyModelHelp: Model used for long texts such as session-log study notes. Leave empty for the default ({{model}}).
general.openrouterKeyHelp: This key shares the store with the OpenRouter key on the Sound tab (either side works). Once saved it stays in the app and is never shown again.
general.summaryTestInstruction: Summarize the following text in one sentence.
general.summaryTestText: This is a test sentence sent from the settings screen to check that the summarizer actually answers. If a summary comes back, both the command and the light model are set correctly.
general.errorSummarizerDisabled: Summaries are turned off (turn them on in the General tab)
general.errorCommandNotFound: Command not found (check that it is installed and that the command field is right)

sound.typingHelp: The keyboard clatter agents make while working.
sound.notifyHelp: The ding on alerts and the session start/end effects.
sound.volumeHelp: Shared by the switches above and by speech.
sound.attentionHoldHelp: Holds a question alert this long; if the agent keeps working in the meantime (auto-approve and such), no alert is raised. 0 alerts immediately.

tts.title: Read alerts aloud (TTS)
tts.help: When a character waits for confirmation or finishes a task, the alert text is turned into a short line in that character's voice and read aloud (bell alerts excluded). The voice follows the character's species and can be picked by hand in the character editor. It spends ElevenLabs credits, so it is off by default.
tts.rewriteHelp: How system text is turned into a character's voice. The claude CLI needs no API key but spends subscription quota. "No rewrite" reads the raw text.
tts.modelOpenrouterHelp: Write the OpenRouter model id as vendor/model. Models missing from the list can be typed in.
tts.modelAnthropicHelp: One-line rewrites, so the default (Haiku) is plenty. Models missing from the list can be typed in.
tts.keyStatus: ElevenLabs key {{elevenlabs}} · Anthropic key {{anthropic}} · OpenRouter key {{openrouter}} · claude CLI {{claudeCli}} → rewrite: {{rewrite}}
tts.elevenlabsKeyHelp: Required for speech. Once saved it stays in the app and is never shown again. Saving with the field empty keeps the existing key — to remove it use the "Delete key" button below (the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY variable also counts as a fallback).
tts.anthropicKeyHelp: Used only for line rewrites. If empty, the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY variable is used, and failing that the claude CLI.
tts.openrouterKeyHelp: Used only when the provider above is OpenRouter. If empty, the OPENROUTER_API_KEY variable is used.
tts.mutedNote: Mute is on, so real alerts are not spoken (previews still are).

system.gitStatusHelp: Looks up each file's git change state (modified, added, deleted…) in "Browse work folder" and shows it as a badge. Turn it off if huge repos feel slow.
system.workdirShowIgnoredHelp: Includes .gitignore'd files and hidden (dot) files in the "Browse work folder" list. With big build outputs (node_modules, target…) the list may hit the 5000-item cap and get truncated. The .git/ directory stays excluded either way.
system.keepAwakeHelp: Keeps the computer from sleeping on its own while a character works. The display may still turn off, and closing the lid or sleeping by hand is not blocked. (macOS, Windows)
system.sessionLogHelp: Records what passed through the terminal (AI turns, commands, output) to a readable text file. Open it from a character tab's right-click "View session log" and turn it into study notes. Logs older than 30 days, or beyond 2GB total, are deleted oldest-first.
system.mascotHelp: Floats the currently active character in a small always-on-top window separate from the app. Alerts show up there, and clicking opens that character's terminal.
system.mascotLightsHelp: Shows a row of status lamps under the mascot, one per target. Off (gray) means no work, green means working, yellow means waiting for your response. In by-project mode, only folders with a session connected to this app light up.
system.mascotLightsFaceHelp: Choose what to show in each lamp's round face. Even with Portrait selected, a character without a portrait falls back to its sprite face.
system.mascotLightsLabelHelp: Choose what name to show under each status lamp. Choosing Task widens the lamps. A lamp with nothing to show for the chosen option (e.g. an agent with no task info) falls back to the default name.
system.usageFloatHelp: Shows a translucent usage panel in the bottom-right when the terminal fills the whole app window. When off, usage is only shown in the bottom bar.
system.sessionCostHelp: Shows the current session's cumulative tokens and an estimated cost (based on public API rates) on the right side of the bar above the terminal. This is an estimate, not your actual subscription bill.
system.externalTerminalHelp: The app used by a terminal tab's right-click "Open in OS terminal". macOS only — ignored elsewhere.
system.externalEditorHelp: The app used to open the .txt from a terminal tab's right-click "View shell output in editor" (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E).
system.fileIndexHelp: Everything (es.exe) is Windows-only and limited to the docs (md) palette; on failure the default scanner is used automatically.
system.terminalThemeHelp: Pins only the terminal colors to a separate palette. On the default (follow theme) the terminal changes with the app theme.

control.title: CLI control (external)
control.help: Opens a local (127.0.0.1) control server so agent-office ctl … or a script can drive this app. Even when on, commands run only after you approve explicitly below (two steps). It is a security surface, so it is off by default.
control.usageIntro: Inside a session terminal you can use it right away:

webRemote.title: Web remote (work from a browser)
webRemote.help: Connect from a browser on your phone or another computer to watch status and drive the terminal. Sessions keep running on this computer; only output and input are relayed. Even when on, a device must be paired and approved, and the browser gets a fixed command set (no settings changes, no bot control). It is a network surface, so it is off by default.
webRemote.bindHelp: Allowing only the Tailscale network lets tailnet (WireGuard) handle encryption. Allowing all networks means plain text on the same LAN.
webRemote.tailnetMissing: Tailscale was not detected — the server is bound to 127.0.0.1 only, so just this computer can reach it. Start Tailscale and restart the app, or change the allowed network.
webRemote.urlIntro: Open this address in a browser
webRemote.pairHint: Pressing Connect in the browser pops a 6-digit code and an approval window in this app. Type that code into the browser (it shows up even with settings closed).
webRemote.notRunning: The server is not up yet — reopen this screen in a moment.
webRemote.serveNoCli: The Tailscale command line tool was not found — connect over the http address above without HTTPS (tailnet encrypts it anyway). Run Install CLI in the Tailscale app to enable it here.
webRemote.serveOnIntro: HTTPS is open. Use this address
webRemote.serveOnNote: Tailscale remembers this mapping — it survives quitting the app and rebooting (with the app closed, only the connection fails). The first connect can take a few seconds for the certificate.
webRemote.serveOffIntro: Register an HTTPS proxy (port {{port}}) with Tailscale to connect over a https:// address. No browser warning, and cookies are issued as Secure.
webRemote.serveConflict: Port {{port}} is already used by something else ({{upstream}}). The app never overwrites someone else's setup — if you do not need that mapping, clear it yourself with the command below.

talk.title: Peer talk (characters talking to each other)
talk.help: Lets a character send a message into another character's session. A conversation starts only when you explicitly invoke the /agent-office:talk skill in a session, and turning this switch off drops even undelivered messages. It types into someone else's session, so it is off by default.
talk.maxTurnsHelp: How many messages one conversation may exchange. Reaching it ends the talk (a guard against two characters going back and forth forever).
talk.idleQuietHelp: The receiving character must be quiet this long before a message is typed into their terminal. While they work it is held back, so a message does not land the instant it is sent.
talk.controlWarn: ⚠ Peer talk runs through CLI control. Turn on “CLI control” above and approve it — right now it is {{reason}}, so every attempt to talk will fail.
talk.skillNote: Start a talk inside a session with /agent-office:talk — the app installs the skill for you, so there is nothing to set up.

firstRun.title: Welcome to Agent Office
firstRun.intro: The Claude Code / Codex / Pi integrations are optional. You can start with them off and turn them on any time from ⚙ in the bottom bar.

pairing.title: Connection request
pairing.request: {{name}} (web browser) wants to connect to this office.
pairing.enterCode: Type this code into the browser:
pairing.warn: Reject it if you do not recognize the request. Approving lets it watch your characters' terminals and run a fixed set of commands.

modelPicker.failed: Could not load the list — you can type a model id yourself.
modelPicker.empty: No matching model — you can use it as typed.
